mainTopic: רב הונא and the returned basket, whether ניצוק is a חיבור, the six-year-old's ruling on treading grapes with a נכרי, and שמואל's delayed ruling in נהרדעא
overview: The amud opens by closing the earlier discussion. Since רבא does not treat wine as a special case, he reads the sources as a dispute among three תנאים. Next the גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that only the wine already in the collection vat (בור) is forbidden. רב הונא limits this rule: if the wicker basket (גרגותני) is put back into the winepress, the wine left in the press becomes forbidden too. The גמרא tries to prove from this that a poured stream (ניצוק) joins two liquids. It rejects that proof with רבי חייא's case of the flask: the vat may simply have filled up until it touched the basket. Then comes the story of a brilliant six-year-old who ruled that one may tread grapes with a נכרי if his hands are tied, because touching wine with the foot is not ניסוך. Finally, the גמרא tells of a case in נהרדעא where a Jew and a נכרי trod wine together, and שמואל held off ruling for three רגלים. The גמרא begins to ask why he waited, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How רבא explains the earlier dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion: since רבא does not treat wine as a special case, he must read the sources as a dispute among three תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, who does not say that wine is different, he explains it as following three תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the previous discussion by explaining how רבא would read the sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another approach solved the earlier contradiction by saying that wine used for ניסוך is a special case. רבא does not accept that difference, so he has to say that the different משניות follow different תנאים. That leaves three separate opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different, a special case
He sets it up, he explains it as
Three תנאים (three different opinions)

phrases.english: And according to Rava, for whom it is not different,
phrases.notes: "It" is the case of wine used for ניסוך, which another approach treated as a special case.

phrases.english: he explains it as following three tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרָבָא, דְּלָא שָׁאנֵי לֵיהּ, מוֹקֵים לֵיהּ כִּתְלָתָא תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבא, the sources reflect three different תנאים, not a special rule for wine.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the משנה: the returned basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that only the wine in the vat is forbidden. רב הונא says this is true only if the straining basket was not put back into the winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: what is in the vat is forbidden and the rest is permitted. רב הונא said: this was taught only if he did not return the wicker basket to the winepress. But if he returned the basket to the winepress, the rest is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. Then רב הונא adds a limit to that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that once the wine flows down into the vat, only the vat's wine becomes forbidden, while the wine still in the press stays permitted. רב הונא says that if the basket, which held wine connected to the vat, is put back into the press, it forbids the wine in the press too.

keyTerms.meaning: The collection vat (pit) below the winepress
The winepress where the grapes are trodden
Wicker basket used to strain the wine on its way to the vat
They taught this only in the case of (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: What is in the vat is forbidden, and the rest is permitted.
Rav Huna said:
They taught this only
where he did not return the wicker basket to the winepress,
but if he returned the wicker basket to the winepress, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the משנה's rule about the vat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the basket is returned to the winepress, the wine remaining in the winepress becomes forbidden too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that forbidden wine can spread to permitted wine through a connected object.

steps.title: How did the basket's wine become forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the wine in the basket itself became forbidden in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The basket itself, by what does it become forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רב הונא's rule, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule only works if the basket's wine is already forbidden. Only the vat's wine was made forbidden, so the גמרא wants to know what linked the basket to the vat.

keyTerms.meaning: By what? How?
It becomes forbidden

phrases.english: The wicker basket itself, by what does it become forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis for רב הונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What connects the basket's wine to the forbidden wine in the vat?

steps.title: Proof that a poured stream connects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the basket becomes forbidden through the stream flowing down into the vat, and concludes that a poured stream (ניצוק) counts as a connection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through the stream. Learn from this: a poured stream is a connection!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a likely answer and then tries to prove a general rule from רב הונא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only link between the basket and the vat seems to be the stream of wine pouring from one into the other. If that stream makes the basket forbidden, then a stream must join the two liquids into one. That would settle the well-known question of ניצוק חיבור.

keyTerms.meaning: A stream of liquid being poured from one container to another
A connection that joins two things into one unit
Learn from this (introduces a proof)

phrases.english: Through the stream.
phrases.notes: The wine running down from the basket into the vat keeps them joined.

phrases.english: Learn from this: a poured stream is a connection!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question and draws a proof from the answer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling about the returned basket.

steps.title: Rejected: the vat filled up to the basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Like רבי חייא's case of the flask, רב הונא may mean that the vat's wine rose until it actually touched the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: where his flask filled up and reached it. Here too: where his vat filled up and reached it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by offering a different way the basket could have become forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא taught that wine in a funnel becomes forbidden when the נכרי's flask fills up until it touches the funnel. In the same way, רב הונא may mean the vat filled up until its wine touched the basket. Then there is direct contact, so nothing is proven about a stream.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught (in a ברייתא)
It filled up and reached it
Flask
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not decide here that ניצוק is NOT a חיבור. It only shows that רב הונא's rule cannot prove it either way.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
where his flask filled up and reached it.
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא's case of pouring wine through a funnel into a נכרי's flask; the flask's wine rose up to the funnel.

phrases.english: Here too: where his vat filled up and reached it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that ניצוק is a חיבור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The basket may be forbidden through direct contact when the vat fills up, not through the stream.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: a basket returned to the winepress forbids the rest of the wine. This does not prove ניצוק חיבור, since the vat may have filled up and touched the basket.

steps.title: The six-year-old is asked about treading with a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells of a child who learned מסכת עבודה זרה at age six. People asked him if one may tread grapes in a winepress together with a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain child who learned עבודה זרה at six years old was asked: May one tread grapes in the winepress with a נכרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story and sets up a question that the child will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Treading grapes with a נכרי seems risky, because the נכרי might make the wine forbidden. The question is whether a Jew may do this work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A child
They asked him
To tread (press grapes with the feet)
A non-Jew

phrases.english: A certain child
who learned Avodah Zarah at six years old,
they asked him:
What is the law about treading with the non-Jew in the winepress?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יָנוֹקָא דִּתְנָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּשֵׁית שְׁנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story on a related winepress question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it permitted to tread grapes with a נכרי in the winepress?

steps.title: The child permits treading with a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The child answers that one may tread grapes with a נכרי in the winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: One may tread with the נכרי in the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The child gives his ruling: it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives a plain yes without any conditions. The next questions will test how this can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: One may tread

phrases.english: He said to them:
One may tread with the non-Jew in the winepress.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דּוֹרְכִין עִם הַנׇּכְרִי בַּגַּת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Treading with a נכרי is permitted.

steps.title: But he makes it a libation with his hands
steps.stepSummary: They challenge the child: the נכרי will touch the wine with his hands and make it יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he makes it a libation with his hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners attack the child's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a נכרי touches wine with his hand, it can become יין נסך and forbidden. Then the Jew could not benefit from his work, so how can treading be allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
Makes wine into a libation for עבודה זרה

phrases.english: But doesn't he make it a libation with his hand?

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that treading with a נכרי is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נכרי's hand touches the wine and makes it יין נסך.

steps.title: We tie his hands
steps.stepSummary: The child answers that the נכרי's hands are tied, so he cannot touch the wine with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The child answers the challenge by limiting his ruling to a case where the hands are tied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With his hands tied, the נכרי cannot do ניסוך with them. So the problem of the hands is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: We tie, we bind

phrases.english: We tie his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the hands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to allow treading with a נכרי in any case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is allowed when the נכרי's hands are tied.

steps.title: But he makes it a libation with his foot
steps.stepSummary: They challenge again: the נכרי's feet are in the wine while treading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he makes it a libation with his foot!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners push further with a second challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying the hands does not help with the feet, which touch the wine the whole time he treads. So the wine should still become forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Foot

phrases.english: But doesn't he make it a libation with the foot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer about tying the hands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that tying the hands solves the problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The feet still touch the wine during treading.

steps.title: Touching with the foot is not a libation
steps.stepSummary: The child answers that touching wine with the foot is not considered ניסוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: A libation with the foot is not called a libation.
steps.whatsHappening: The child gives his final answer, which ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניסוך is done with the hand, not the foot. So the feet touching the wine does not make it forbidden, and with tied hands treading is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Making wine into a libation for עבודה זרה
Is not called, does not count as

steps.whatToRemember: One may tread grapes with a נכרי if his hands are tied, because touching wine with the foot is not ניסוך.

phrases.english: A libation with the foot is not called a libation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the foot.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any touch by the נכרי, even with the foot, makes the wine forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only touching with the hand counts as ניסוך; the foot does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a practical rule: a נכרי's foot touching wine does not make it יין נסך.

steps.title: The incident in נהרדעא: שמואל delays his ruling
steps.stepSummary: A Jew and a נכרי trod wine together in נהרדעא, and שמואל held off ruling for three רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in נהרדעא where a Jew and a נכרי trod a batch of wine together. שמואל held off ruling on it for three festivals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that matches the case of treading wine with a נכרי. It sets up a question about why שמואל did not rule right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a נכרי actually trod the wine with a Jew. That raises the question of whether the wine became יין נסך. שמואל did not rule for a long time, and that delay is what the גמרא will now look into.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case that happened
נהרדעא, a city in Babylonia where שמואל lived
They trod (pressed grapes with their feet)
Wine
He delayed it, held off ruling on it
Festivals (the three רגלים)

phrases.english: There was a certain incident in Neharde'a,
where a Jew and a gentile trod
a certain wine,
and Shmuel delayed it for three Festivals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that matches the treading scenario discussed in steps 7-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of wine trodden by a Jew and a נכרי, שמואל delayed his ruling for three festivals.

steps.title: Why did שמואל delay?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made שמואל hold off ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל waited so long instead of ruling right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting three festivals suggests that something about the case was unclear to שמואל. The גמרא wants to know which point was in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the delay described in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What doubt caused שמואל to delay ruling on the wine for three festivals?

steps.title: A first suggested reason begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to suggest a reason for שמואל's delay: "If we say it was because he held..."
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it is because he held:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a first guess about שמואל's reasoning. The guess itself comes in the next line, so this step only sets up that next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אילימא introduces a possible explanation. Very often the גמרא raises such a guess only to test it and then reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
He holds, he is of the opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat this as the final answer. אילימא usually brings a suggestion that the גמרא will push back on.

phrases.english: If we say it is because he held:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a suggested answer to the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first, tentative explanation of שמואל's reasoning is being introduced. Its content continues in the next line.
